history.dynasty: Within the Simhachalam complex whose recorded history spans Chola (1087 CE), Eastern Ganga (13th century) and Vijayanagara (16th century). A 1293 CE inscription records Ganga-era sub-shrines dedicated to Vishnu manifestations (Vaikunthanatha, Yagnavaraha, Madhavadevara).
history.summary: PROVISIONAL RECORD (flag): no independent web source found that names a 'Kasi Vishweswara' sub-shrine within the Simhachalam temple complex - this row is documented as a sub-shrine of the main complex (row 1231) and its existence/identity needs on-site verification. The Simhachalam complex does have Shaivite-tinged sub-shrines (a 1293 CE inscription records Ganga-era sub-shrines; the Tripurantaka kshetrapala shrine stands on the way to Gangadhara; the sandalwood-covered deity itself resembles a Shiva lingam). NOTE: a Kasi Viswanatha sub-shrine is independently documented in the Srikalahasti temple complex (rows 1233-1234) - possible CSV misattribution to Simhachalam; verify before display. Coordinates are those of the main Simhachalam complex (same as row 1231); the sub-shrine's exact position is unverified.

name: Kasi Vishweswara Sub-shrine, Simhachalam Temple Complex
town_description: Simhachalam is a hill suburb of Visakhapatnam in the Simhachalam hill range of the Eastern Ghats, about 300 metres above sea level. Part of the Greater Visakhapatnam municipal area, it is reached by a winding ghat road and draws pilgrims year-round to the hilltop temple complex, one of the 32 Narasimha Kshetras of Andhra Pradesh.
tradition: Shaivism (sub-shrine within a predominantly Vaishnavite complex)

travel.road: APSRTC buses from Visakhapatnam RTC Complex (~20 km); scenic uphill ghat road to the hilltop (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March are the most preferred months to visit (verify)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Same as the main Simhachalam temple complex: 7:00 AM - 4:00 PM and 6:00 PM - 9:00 PM (verify)
